Competitor News.title: Standard Chartered and F1 ACADEMY Launch 'Drive Further' Financial Skills Initiative
Competitor News.summary: Standard Chartered and F1 ACADEMY Launch 'Drive Further' Financial Skills Initiative FF News
Competitor News.copy:
Standard Chartered has partnered with F1 ACADEMY to launch ‘Drive Further,’ a multi-year financial literacy initiative for female racing drivers. By providing training in sponsorship, budgeting, and investment, the programme addresses the commercial complexities of professional motorsport, ensuring athletes possess the financial acumen required to manage their careers as effectively as their performance on the track.

The "Drive Further" initiative is a multi-year programme designed to equip female drivers with the practical financial and commercial skills necessary to sustain a career in professional motorsport. Developed in response to needs identified by the drivers themselves, the curriculum focuses on areas where young athletes often face significant pressure, including sponsorship acquisition, financial planning, budgeting, and investment strategies. The programme combines virtual learning modules with in-person workshops and personalised support, leveraging the banking and wealth management expertise of Standard Chartered.

Wider Sports News.copy: FIFA has advanced its bidding process for U.S. media rights to the 2030 Men’s World Cup to a second round, with the world governing body “aiming to create a bidding war between Netflix and Fox Sports/Univision.” Sources said Netflix “submitted the largest bid before last week’s deadline and are now regarded as frontrunners,” with FIFA understood to have “invited second bids in an attempt to drive up the price.” Asking for a second bid is “not unusual in a media rights tender even when there is a clear leader in the first round,” which “appears to be the case in this instance.” Netflix is understood to have “initially trumped offers” from Amazon and the joint bid from Fox and Spanish-language broadcaster Univision. The four nations are the only bidders, and member associations will vote at a specially arranged virtual meeting while a UK delegation attends Fifa’s Zurich headquarters. Rugby.title: Two teams face Nations Championship relegation under 2030 playoff plans
Rugby.summary: Two teams face Nations Championship relegation under 2030 playoff plans The Guardian
Rugby.copy:
Two teams could be relegated from the Nations Championship from 2030 under controversial plans being developed by the tournament organisers. The Guardian has learned that the favoured mechanism for introducing relegation is for the bottom sides in the northern and southern hemisphere tables to face a one-legged playoff match against the winners of the equivalent tables in the tier-two Nations Cup, which is run by World Rugby. The tier one sides would be guaranteed home advantage in the tie, which based on this year’s inaugural competition would see matches between Italy and Georgia and Fiji and the USA, with the winner of each securing a place in the Nations Championship two years later.

The introduction of two relegation playoffs would see an extra match added to the final series, the first of which begins on Friday at the Allianz Stadium, with the bottom-ranked sides Italy and Fiji opening proceedings before the third v third game between Ireland and Australia.

Rugby.title: Two teams to be cut as Rugby Europe confirm 2028 restructure
Rugby.summary: Rugby Europe has unveiled a new format for the men's senior competitions that will take effect in 2028.
Rugby.copy:
Rugby Europe has unveiled a new format for the men’s senior competitions that will take effect in 2028. The Men’s Rugby Europe Championship will resize back to six teams, played in a single round-robin format. This restructuring means the two teams that finish at the bottom will be automatically relegated after the next edition, which Portugal, Georgia, Spain, Romania, the Netherlands, Belgium, Switzerland, and Poland will contest. The tournament will begin in February with two groups of four teams (Georgia, Romania, Switzerland, and Belgium in Group A; and Portugal, Spain, the Netherlands, and Switzerland in Group B), followed by semi-finals and a final.

This marks a return to a format in place for nearly two decades, discontinued in early 2020 when the Championship expanded to eight teams and introduced a knockout stage. In recent years, Badajoz, Paris, and Madrid have hosted the finals, and now Bucharest will have the honour of holding this finals format one last time.

Rugby.title: Cowan-Dickie insists England will not let up after record triumph over All Blacks
Rugby.summary: Cowan-Dickie insists England will not let up after record triumph over All Blacks The Guardian
Rugby.copy:
Luke Cowan-Dickie is adamant England will not let complacency creep in after their record win over the All Blacks, insisting they will not repeat the mistakes of the 2019 World Cup.

Cowan-Dickie is one of three players, with Jamie George and Maro Itoje, who would claim a fourth career win for England against New Zealand on Saturday if Steve Borthwick’s side back up last weekend’s 37-12 victory at Twickenham. The Sale hooker was part of the squad who defeated the All Blacks in the 2019 World Cup semi-final in emphatic fashion and went into the final against South Africa as favourites. Eddie Jones’s side were comfortably outplayed by the Springboks, however, with Cowan-Dickie acknowledging that England failed to hit their emotional peak that day.

Rugby.title: Dan Sheehan learns his fate after 'Croc Roll' hearing
Rugby.summary: The Ireland captain's international season is over after red card is upheld.
Rugby.copy:
Ireland’s stand-in captain Dan Sheehan has been banned for two matches for the croc roll that earned him a red card against South Africa last weekend. Sheehan, who started at No.8 for the first time in his 42-cap Ireland career in the 20-17 win, was sin-binned for the act of foul play on South Africa’s Marco van Staden, before the yellow card was later upgraded by the Foul Player Review Officer. Van Staden also suffered the same fate after originally being sin-binned for retaliation.

The Foul Play Review Committee met in London on Tuesday and upheld the red card but deemed it worthy of low-entry level sanction. Sheehan will now miss the Nations Championship fifth-place play-off against Australia at Allianz Stadium on Friday, as well as Leinster’s URC trip to Ospreys in the United Rugby Championship, on 4 December.

Rugby.title: Sheehan out of Wallabies Test after two-game ban
Rugby.summary: Ireland's stand-in captain Dan Sheehan will be banned for two games after a croc-roll tackle against South Africa and will play no part against Australia on Friday night.
Rugby.copy:
Ireland's stand-in captain Dan Sheehan has been banned for two games after a croc-roll tackle against South Africa and will play no part against Australia on Friday night. The Leinster forward was shown a yellow card by referee Christophe Ridley in the 72nd minute of Ireland's 20-17 victory over the Springboks in Dublin on Saturday.

That was later upgraded to a red card by the foul play review officer (FPRO) on the basis of World Rugby's Law 9.20d that "a player may remove the jackler from the tackle area by pushing/driving them backwards (including by grabbing the knee/leg), but must not roll, pull or twist an opponent".

Rugby.title: Wallabies win over Wales far from perfect – but a lot better than recent weeks
Rugby.summary: Australia's display in Cardiff was not without fault, but it was a welcome boost at a time of year when other northern campaigns have come undone.
Rugby.copy:
There have been times in the last six or seven weeks where Australian rugby fans have wondered when – or if – the next Wallabies win might come. The Bledisloe Cup losses weren’t much fun, and there was a more than fair argument that the England and Scotland defeats, to start the November leg of the Nations Championship, were even worse. And knowing the Wallabies’ last two European tours both ended with a run of losses, it’s reasonable to assume that Australian confidence has taken a hit in recent times.

So it was pleasing to see the Wallabies start so well against Wales in Cardiff, adjust to the inevitable reactions, and complete the job at hand. Having spent the week celebrating maybe their greatest ever win, Wales were always going to be a tough prospect; the only unknowns were how much that masterful, but exhausting, win over New Zealand – and the aforementioned celebrations – had taken out of the Welsh players.

Rugby.title: Steve Borthwick hits rewind button to inspire England’s flying starts
Rugby.summary: Steve Borthwick hits rewind button to inspire England’s flying starts The Guardian
Rugby.copy:
Ellis Genge was so fired up by England’s powerful response to the haka on Saturday he stripped off his anthem jacket in the aftermath, completely forgetting he was not starting. Ollie Chessum told Lewis Moody, who had been invited to stand at the point of England’s V formation: “We are going long left, stay on the field and chase the kick-off.” And according to Ben Earl, who would still be out on the Twickenham turf carrying through traffic if he could, some players were so inspired by Moody’s speech the night before they could not sleep.

Against that emotional backdrop, it is small wonder England flew out of the blocks against the All Blacks. Steve Borthwick has spoken a lot about “bringing the fire” recently and on Saturday they torched the place, riding the emotional wave that Moody’s presence inspired from Henry Slade’s fourth-minute try, through to a record victory against New Zealand.

Rugby.summary: Former England captain Lewis Moody joins the current team to face New Zealand's haka in an emotional start to Saturday's Test match at Allianz Stadium.
Rugby.copy:
Former England captain Lewis Moody joined the current team to face New Zealand's haka in an emotional start to Saturday's Test match at Allianz Stadium. Moody, who was diagnosed with motor neurone disease (MND) last year, stood at the centre of England's line-up - between captain Maro Itoje and one of the team's vice-captains, Ellis Genge - as they faced up to the traditional pre-match challenge.

Led by Genge's fellow vice-captains Ollie Chessum and Jamie George, England then advanced to form a V shape, similar to the formation they took before last year's victory and the 2019 Rugby World Cup semi-final win against the All Blacks.

However, with the tournament set to move from the Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Super 300 category to Super 100 from 2027, questions have emerged over its standing in the international badminton calendar. Pitchamon, the 2023 world junior champion, had earlier been provisionally suspended. She missed the Asian Games for Thailand. Furosemide is a diuretic, sometimes called a “water pill,” used to treat fluid retention and high blood pressure. It is prohibited in sport because it can mask the use of other banned substances or cause rapid weight loss through fluid loss.

Racket.copy:
Alexander Zverev has described comments that ATP Tour chairman Andrea Gaudenzi made about players playing through pain as “unfair.” At a press conference during the ATP Finals in Turin last week, Gaudenzi said current players are “smart” at managing injuries and suggested they use painkillers less often than his generation.

“I think I played the last seven years of my career with painkillers, and I broke my shoulder here in Milan in Davis Cup final because I took a cortisone injection six weeks before the final,” said the Italian, who played on the ATP Tour between 1990 and 2003.

Racket.title: “Unfair comment” – Alexander Zverev Bluntly Calls Out ATP Chairman After ‘Painkiller’ Comment On Hectic Schedule Sparks Controversy
Racket.summary: “Unfair comment” – Alexander Zverev Bluntly Calls Out ATP Chairman After ‘Painkiller’ Comment On Hectic Schedule Sparks Controversy Yahoo Sports
Racket.copy:
Alexander Zverev took a jab at ATP chairman Andrea Gaudenzi over his comments about players' use of painkillers amid the demanding tennis schedule. Gaudenzi recently claimed that modern players are better at managing their physical condition and depend less on painkillers than the players did when he competed. He also recalled relying on painkillers during the seven years of his career and added that players in the past often competed despite injuries. Gaudenzi's comments came amid growing concerns about the demanding tennis calendar and its increasing toll on players.

However, his opinions did not land well with Zverev, who, during the press conference ahead of the Davis Cup, called out Gaudenzi. The German tennis player stated that it was unfair of the ATP chairman because he had no idea how many painkillers players actually take. Zverev further mentioned that he was much healthier this year compared to last year, when he struggled with back and bone problems before finding the medication to manage them.

Racket.title: India To Host 2028 Thomas And Uber Cup Finals In New Delhi
Racket.summary: India To Host 2028 Thomas And Uber Cup Finals In New Delhi Sportscape Magazine
Racket.copy:
New Delhi will host the 2028 Thomas and Uber Cup Finals. See India's record in both cups, what BAI said, and whether the capital's venue is ready. The Badminton World Federation (BWF) has awarded New Delhi the hosting rights for the 2028 Thomas and Uber Cup Finals, the men’s and women’s world teams championship. The Badminton Association of India (BAI) announced this on 25 November 2026, after successfully hosting the 2026 BWF World Championships in New Delhi in August. The World Championship held at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium welcomed more than 400 players from over 50 nations. The Thomas and Uber Cup is the third major BWF tournament that India has landed in three years, after the 2025 World Junior Championships in Guwahati. The 2028 finals return to India after 14 years, since 2014.

Commenting on the announcement, BAI President Dr. Himanta Biswa Sarma said, “Over the past few years, we at BAI have worked to make India a partner the BWF can count on to stage its biggest events. China has played that role for many years, and India has now earned that same trust. Our players have raised India’s standing on court, winning the Thomas Cup in 2022 and taking bronze in 2026. As a federation, we have built the organisational capacity and mobilised the financial resources needed to deliver championships of this scale.”

Jodar, who began the season at No.165 in the world, finishes it at No.10, having climbed a staggering 155 spots across the 2026 season. Eight-time Grand Slam champion Andre Agassi previously held the distinction, having climbed 104 spots from No.110 to No.6 in 1998.

bullets: The BWF has confirmed the top eight qualifiers in each of five events for the HSBC BWF World Tour Finals in Hangzhou, China, from 9 to 13 December, after the Hong Kong Open ended on 22 November. The prize pot is US$3.5 million, the biggest of the season.

Racket.copy:
The BWF World Tour Finals 2026 field is set for Hangzhou. See all qualifiers in five events, including India's PV Sindhu and Lakshya Sen, and the USD 3.5 million prize pot. The Badminton World Federation (BWF) has released the list of the top eight qualifiers in the singles and doubles categories for the HSBC BWF World Tour Finals 2026. The list was confirmed after the Hong Kong Open ended on Sunday, 22 November. India has two entries in the World Finals qualifiers in the singles category, World No.6 PV Sindhu and World No.11 Lakshya Sen. Lakshya got in after Koki Watanabe lost in the first round, which also helped Chou Tien Chen and Kunlavut Vitidsarn. Sindhu qualified earlier after winning the Hylo Open 2026 in Germany.

An Se Young, the world champion, is one title away from a record of 12 titles in a season. Intanon earned a record 11th Finals qualification, and Sindhu is described as resurgent.

Racket.title: The line between sports hero and gambling shill is fast disappearing
Racket.summary: For big stars, endorsing companies like Kalshi and Polymarket is just another day in the beautiful business of being – and staying – rich When Giannis Antetokounmpo announced he was taking an investment stake in prediction market Kalshi in February, the claim he made to accompany the announcement – “We all on Kalshi now” – sounded as absurd as the howls of outrage from sports lovers seemed universal. Nine months later, Kalshi’s grip on American fans appears murderously tight: notional monthly trading volume on the platform, the majority of which is taken up by wagers on sports, increased to nearly $100bn in October from $40bn in August, as the company gears up for yet another funding round at a rumored valuation of $65bn ahead of a potential IPO. Rival prediction market Polymarket, which relaunched in the US late last year after regulators shut it down in 2022, has seen similar growth over recent months. However righteous the disgust from fans on social media at the deepening incursion of these odious platforms into professional sport may be, their popularity seems only to grow. More perplexing is the widening circle of athletes like Giannis who’ve thrown off whatever shame might once have come from association with these businesses and given them their full-throated support. The line between role model and shill in professional sports is now essentially non-existent. Pete Sampras, a man so private in retirement it can often seem like his entire tennis career was a collective hallucination, released an ad for Kalshi during this year’s US Open after two decades largely out of the public eye. José Mourinho trousered a brick of Kalshi cash this summer in exchange for a gambling promo during the World Cup. The prediction market machine now sponsors Jalen Brunson and Josh Hart’s Roommates Show, on which the recently crowned pair of NBA champions begin every episode dutifully informing us that their amazingly dreary podcast is “presented by Polymarket, the top prediction market”. LeBron James will make more from his recently announced partnership with Polymarket – $15m a year – than he will from playing for the Philadelphia 76ers. Somehow we’ve arrived at the point where it’s bigger news if a professional athlete takes a firm stand against the prediction markets, as Victor Wembanyama recently did , rather than pockets the cash to endorse them. Racket.title: Alcaraz outplays Zverev for first ATP Finals triumph
Racket.summary: Carlos Alcaraz ends his wait for a first ATP Finals title as he outplays world number one Alexander Zverev in Turin.
bullets: Carlos Alcaraz beat world number one Alexander Zverev 6-2 7-6 (9-7) to win his first ATP Finals title. It was the 23-year-old's 14th successive win and third straight title, and made him the youngest man to win all four Grand Slams and the Finals.

Alcaraz returned at the US Open in August after more than four months out with a wrist issue, and has won 21 of 22 matches since. In the doubles, Theo Arribage and Albano Olivetti beat Marcelo Arevalo and Mate Pavic 3-6 7-6 (7-2) 10-6.
Racket.copy:
Carlos Alcaraz outplayed world number one Alexander Zverev to end his wait for a first ATP Finals title and complete a remarkable post-injury return to the sport. A season which began with Alcaraz becoming the youngest man to complete the career Grand Slam, before he was ruled out for more than four months with a wrist issue, ended with the Spaniard holding aloft another of the sport's biggest trophies.

Alcaraz, still wearing heavy strapping around his upper-left leg following his injury scare earlier in the week, collapsed to the ground in celebration after sealing a 6-2 7-6 (9-7) win in a dramatic second-set tie-break.

Golf.title: Is Wyndham Clark signing with PING? | Special Tour Report
Golf.summary: What drivers are Brooks Koepka, Justin Thomas, Wyndham Clark and Jackson Koivun using in the Skins Game? One might have a big change in play. The post Is Wyndham Clark signing with PING? | Special Tour Report appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
If you grew up with golf on TV over Thanksgiving weekend, the Skins Game probably rings a bell. It started in 1983 at Desert Highlands in Scottsdale, Arizona, with about as big a foursome as golf could put together: Jack Nicklaus, Arnold Palmer, Gary Player and Tom Watson.

The rules are simple. Every hole is worth money, and when nobody wins a hole outright, the money rolls over to the next. Fred Couples won it so often he got the nickname “Mr. Skins.” The event disappeared after 2008, then came back on Black Friday last year. This year’s foursome is all new. Brooks Koepka is a five-time major champion trying to get back on track after leaving LIV. Two-time PGA Championship winner Justin Thomas is bringing his comedy back to our screens, Wyndham Clark is coming off a season where he’s been debated as the player of the year, and Jackson Koivun is a 21-year-old rookie who beat Scottie Scheffler to win the 3M Open just a few months ago. They’re playing for $4 million at Atlantic Fields Club in Hobe Sound, Florida.

Golf.copy:

Editor’s note: This is Part 3 in a three-part series from the PGA Tour and Cleveland Clinic offering a behind-the-scenes look at today’s modern approach to player health and performance. This series explores what players can access inside the PGA Tour Performance Truck presented by Cleveland Clinic, how Cleveland Clinic experts use testing and insights to identify potential issues before they become injuries and how a comprehensive approach to health can help players stay competitive longer.

Golf.title: Brooks Koepka rule improves pro's PGA Tour status for 2027
Golf.summary: Brooks Koepka's return from LIV Golf benefitted many PGA Tour pros in 2026, including Max McGreevy on the last day of the season. The post Brooks Koepka rule improves pro’s PGA Tour status for 2027 appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
Max McGreevy had just emptied the tank on the final day of the PGA Tour season. After a year in which he made 19 of 31 cuts but failed to produce any stellar results, the 31-year-old had needed to put together a good final round at the RSM Classic to give himself a chance at retaining some semblance of PGA Tour status.

But an even-par 70 at Sea Island left McGreevy tied for 10th. It was his best finish of the season but one that didn’t seem like it was going to be good enough to nudge him inside the top 125 to keep conditional status on the PGA Tour. When McGreevy walked off the course, he was bouncing between No. 126 and 127 in the FedEx Cup Fall standings. Those few spots are a huge difference — between getting 15-20 PGA Tour starts, as Lanto Griffin did in 2026 (17 starts) after finishing 125th last year, or largely plying your trade on the Korn Ferry Tour, as Frankie Capan III (only six PGA Tour starts), who finished 127th in 2025, did this year.

Golf.copy:
The PGA Tour on Tuesday announced nominees for the two major awards it hands out each year, Player of the Year and Rookie of the Year. Scottie Scheffler, Cameron Young, Wyndham Clark, Matt Fitzpatrick and Chris Gotterup make up the five-man race for the Jack Nicklaus Award, while Alex Fitzpatrick, Ben James, Kristoffer Reitan, Jackson Koivun and Marco Penge are among those vying for the Arnold Palmer Award.

Scheffler has become familiar with getting his hands on the Jack Nicklaus Award in recent years. The world No. 1 joined Tiger Woods as the only golfer to claim the title three years in a row when he secured the honor in 2024. After winning it again in 2025, Scheffler can join Woods again as the only players to ever win it five times in a row. The 15-time major champion won the award five straight seasons from 1999-2003 and three straight from 2005-07.

Golf.title: LIV Golf Creditors Threaten Chapter 7 Liquidation Over $2M Offer
Golf.summary: LIV Golf Creditors Threaten Chapter 7 Liquidation Over $2M Offer Front Office Sports
Golf.copy:
LIV Golf’s Chapter 11 bankruptcy case in New Jersey is at risk of being converted to a Chapter 7 liquidation process. The official committee of unsecured creditors in LIV’s case does not support the current wind-down plan, which is offering just $2 million for general recovery claims. “At present, the plan only benefits the debtors’ current and former directors and officers and the Public Investment Fund of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia,” the committee wrote in a statement and reservation of rights filed Monday evening.

A Dec. 4 deadline has been set by the creditors and LIV to reach a deal or “immediately move to convert these cases to Chapter 7 and conduct an orderly liquidation of their assets.” In the meantime, settlement negotiations between all parties are underway. The creditors committee did not object to conditional approval of LIV’s revised disclosure statement and wind-down plan, which was granted by Judge Michael Kaplan on Tuesday morning.

Golf.summary: Marco Penge claims maiden PGA Tour win: Englishman triumphs from four-way playoff at RSM Classic Sky Sports
bullets: England's Marco Penge won his first PGA Tour title at the season-ending RSM Classic, emerging from a four-way playoff with Haotong Li, Michael Thorbjornsen and Max Greyserman, all on 16 under. He birdied the 18th again in the playoff after hitting his approach to 10 feet.

Penge, a three-time DP World Tour winner, needed a top-four finish to keep his PGA Tour card after a rookie season disrupted by viral illness. His final-round 65 earned the playoff place. The DP World Tour's BMW Australian PGA Championship begins on Thursday.
Golf.copy:
English golfer Marco Penge claimed a stunning maiden win on the PGA Tour as he emerged victorious from a four-way playoff at the season-ending RSM Classic. Penge, a three-time winner on the DP World Tour, had gone into the tournament at risk of losing his PGA Tour card for next year after a rookie season disrupted by a viral illness placed him outside of the top 100.

With a top-four finish required to retain his spot, the 28-year-old found form at the best possible time at the Sea Island Golf Club this week, and a final-round 65 earned him a spot alongside Haotong Li of China and Americans Michael Thorbjornsen and Max Greyserman in a playoff decider - all four locked at 16 under.

Golf.title: The PGA Tour season will end without fans. Davis Love III defended the controversial decision
Golf.summary: The Monday finish for the RSM Classic won't have fans. On Sunday, tournament host Davis Love III explained the controversial decision. The post The PGA Tour season will end without fans. Davis Love III defended the controversial decision appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
A lot will be on the line on Monday at Sea Island Resort when the 2026 PGA Tour season concludes. Players will be fighting to keep their PGA Tour cards, jump into the AON Next 10 or trying to secure the first win of their PGA Tour career.

But no one will be there to see the RSM Classic finish. After Saturday’s third round was washed out by rain, the tournament announced it would finish on Monday, but no fans would be allowed on the ground. Fans with Sunday tickets were allowed to watch the golf on Sunday, but Saturday tickets were not honored and fans were asked to see the refund policy since no crowds will be allowed on Monday.

Golf.title: LPGA Tour: Jeeno Thitikul wins CME Group Tour Championship again and overtakes Annika Sorenstam's career money record
Golf.summary: LPGA Tour: Jeeno Thitikul wins CME Group Tour Championship again and overtakes Annika Sorenstam's career money record Sky Sports
Golf.copy:
Jeeno Thitikul has won the LPGA Tour's season-ending CME Group Tour Championship for a third consecutive year after storming to a two-shot victory in Florida. Thitikul carded an eagle and five birdies during an impressive seven-under 65, pulling her clear of a congested leaderboard at Tiburon Golf Club and securing a 12th LPGA Tour title.

She finished on 24 under and two clear of Aki Iwai, who raced into contention with six birdies in the first 10 holes of her final-round 65, while world No 1 Nelly Korda finished in third spot.

Golf.title: Thitikul wins third title in a row at LPGA finale
Golf.summary: World number two Jeeno Thitikul produces a seven-under final round of 65 to claim a third successive CME Group Tour Championship title.
bullets: Jeeno Thitikul won a third successive CME Group Tour Championship with a final-round 65, finishing on 24 under at Tiburon Golf Club in Florida. The world number two took the $4m top prize, two shots ahead of Japan's Akie Iwai.

The win made Thitikul the LPGA Tour's all-time prize money leader on $24,292,858, passing Annika Sorenstam. World number one Nelly Korda finished third on 20 under and also moved past Sorenstam into second. England's Lottie Woad ended on 14 under.
Golf.copy:
World number two Jeeno Thitikul produced a seven-under final round of 65 to claim a third successive CME Group Tour Championship title. The 23-year-old from Thailand started the fourth round of the season-ending event with an eagle and went on to card five birdies as she finished on 24 under at the Tiburon Golf Club in Florida.

"The only words I have is not to change the course until I'm retired," said Thitikul. "It's just me and the course, we just are best friends. I think she is my best friend on the tour."

Golf.title: ‘It Threw Off Our Order’: Davis Love III Reveals How LIV Golf Pros Disrupted Team USA's Ryder Cup Order
Golf.summary: ‘It Threw Off Our Order’: Davis Love III Reveals How LIV Golf Pros Disrupted Team USA's Ryder Cup Order Yahoo Sports
Golf.copy:
A Ryder Cup captaincy is usually a queue. Names are pencilled in years ahead, future captains learn the job as assistants, and everyone knows who is next in line. Then LIV Golf walked in and started rubbing names off the list. That is how Davis Love III described the last few years on the Fully Equipped podcast. The former US captain explained how the Saudi-backed league unsettled Team USA's plans from the inside.

"But, you know, you've got to remember LIV Tour has had a huge impact. It wasn't a ripple effect. It was a bomb effect through all of golf. It threw off our order of captains. It left us not knowing if guys were going to be able to play or not. It obviously affected Europe more than us in terms of understanding who was going to get to play, but it threw us off our order. And then, obviously, Tiger threw us off the order a little bit as well," Love III said on the show.

Golf.title: Kim holds one-shot lead at LPGA finale as Korda closes in
Golf.summary: A-Lim Kim holds a slender lead going into the final round of the CME Group Tour Championship, with world number one Nelly Korda among the chasers.
Golf.copy:
South Korea's A-Lim Kim holds a slender lead going into the final round of the CME Group Tour Championship, with world number one Nelly Korda among the chasers. Kim, who held a three-shot overnight lead, carded a third round 69 which included six birdies and three bogeys, with two of those coming on the final three holes, to reach 18 under overall.

"I really focused on my game. Just aim and hit, that's all," said Kim. "Today the wind direction [was a] little tricky, changed a lot, swirly in the air. That's golf." In the chase for the $4m (£3.1m) top prize at the season-ending event, Japan's Yuri Yoshida and Jeeno Thitikul of Thailand are both on 17 under - one shot behind Kim.

Golf.title: PGA Tour season headed for Monday finish after rain washes out Saturday at RSM Classic
Golf.summary: Heavy rains washed out the third round of the RSM Classic on Saturday. The third round will be played on Sunday and the tournament will end on Monday. The post PGA Tour season headed for Monday finish after rain washes out Saturday at RSM Classic appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
The 2026 PGA Tour season will last one day longer than expected. With pouring rain pummeling St. Simons Island, Georgia, the third round of the season-ending RSM Classic was postponed until Sunday. The final round will be played on Monday. It will be the PGA Tour’s third Monday finish of the fall slate.

“Obviously this is seaside golf, the golf course is very flat, the fairways are generally very flat with just a little bit of subtle movement,” PGA Tour chief referee Steve Rintoul told reporters on Saturday about the decision not to play on Saturday. “They’re above the marsh; they’re not sand-based. Even though it’s sea level, a dunes links look here, it’s not sand-based. So we had a lot of water sitting on the surface, especially in pockets in low areas in fairways where, I mentioned earlier, [we] may have a player who’s in the fairway in temporary water and needs to take relief, and that nearest point of relief takes him outside of the fairway. That takes the preferred lies out of his hands, and it just becomes, it’s not equitable when we get to that. So that kind of forced our hand.”

The RSM Classic title - and the hopes of PGA Tour pros battling to secure full playing privileges for 2027 - will not be decided until Monday. Because of “unplayable course conditions” at Sea Island's Seaside Course, no play was possible on Saturday, meaning the third round will now be played on Sunday, with the final round set for Monday.

A statement from the PGA Tour read: "Due to unplayable course conditions at Sea Island Golf Club resulting from inclement weather today, the third round of The RSM Classic will be contested on Sunday, November 22, with the final round to be played on Monday, November 23."

Golf.summary: Haeran Ryu Opens With Bogey-Free 66 at CME Group Tour Championship LPGA
Golf.copy:
Megan McCrea is the Manager of Digital Operations. Megan is in her second year with the LPGA, working with the LPGA and Epson Tours to manage, develop, maintain, and update website content.

NAPLES, Fla. — Haeran Ryu of the Republic of Korea carded a bogey-free 6-under 66 on Thursday to sit T4 after the first round of the CME Group Tour Championship, one shot behind co-leaders Jeeno Thitikul, A Lim Kim and Karis Davidson at Tiburón Golf Club.

Golf.title: Thitikul, Kim and Davidson share CME Group Tour Championship lead
Golf.summary: Thitikul, Kim and Davidson share CME Group Tour Championship lead www.golfpost.com
Golf.copy:
The LPGA Tour's season finale has a crowded leaderboard after the first day. Jeeno Thitikul, A Lim Kim and Karis Davidson each opened the CME Group Tour Championship at Tiburón Golf Club with a 7-under-par 65. They share the lead at -7, one stroke ahead of a nine-player group at -6. With three rounds still to play, very little separates the top of the 60-player field.

Thitikul is the most closely watched of the three co-leaders. The world No. 2 won this event in 2024 and 2025 and arrived in Naples trying to win the Tour Championship for a third year in a row. Her bogey-free-looking start of seven under puts her right in contention, although that bid is still three rounds away from being decided. A Lim Kim of South Korea and Karis Davidson of Australia matched her score, so the opening round produced a three-nation tie between Thailand, Korea and Australia.

Golf.title: LPGA Tour introduce ‘aggressive’ new solution to stop slow play
Golf.summary: LPGA Tour introduce ‘aggressive’ new solution to stop slow play Yahoo
Golf.copy:
The LPGA Tour is tackling pace of play head-on. It's one of the biggest issues fans have with the modern game, as players are often taking around six hours to complete their rounds. And while the PGA Tour has often been criticized for not taking action to speed up the pace of play, the LPGA Tour is attempting to find solutions.

Their latest move is to fine any player who has been put on the clock over 35 times in a year $35,000. That's an extreme measure, considering the previous threshold was 40 holes, and the previous fine was $5,000.

Golf.title: Thitikul Stretches Tiburón Streak to Nine Straight Rounds in the 60s
Golf.summary: Thitikul Stretches Tiburón Streak to Nine Straight Rounds in the 60s www.golfpost.com
Golf.copy:
A Lim Kim has the lead at the CME Group Tour Championship. But the player behind her is the one who has owned Tiburón Golf Club for the past two years. Jeeno Thitikul has won this event in each of the last two years. On Friday in Naples, Florida, she shot 67 in the second round. That made it nine rounds in a row in the 60s for her at this course, and it keeps her in the race for a third straight title.

Thitikul is alone in second place at 12-under 132, three shots behind A Lim Kim. Kim leads at 15-under 129. Two rounds remain in the LPGA Tour's season finale, so the final weekend of the year now has a clear chase story.

Golf.title: LPGA Tour: Charley Hull in CME Group Tour Championship contention as A Lim Kim fires hole-in-one to grab halfway lead
Golf.summary: LPGA Tour: Charley Hull in CME Group Tour Championship contention as A Lim Kim fires hole-in-one to grab halfway lead Sky Sports
Golf.copy:
A Lim Kim fired a hole-in-one on her way to grabbing the halfway lead at the LPGA Tour's season-ending CME Group Tour Championship, where Charley Hull remains in contention. Kim holed her tee shot with a seven iron at the 168-yard par-three 16th, with the Korean adding seven birdies and a lone bogey in a round-of-the-day 64 at Tiburon Golf Club.

The former US Women's Open champion was tied at the top of the leaderboard until her stunning ace and a birdie at the par-five next, which moved Kim to 15 under and three clear of back-to-back defending champion Jeeno Thitikul.

Golf.title: PGA Tour: England's Marco Penge grabs halfway lead at RSM Classic as big names battle to secure FedExCup future
Golf.summary: PGA Tour: England's Marco Penge grabs halfway lead at RSM Classic as big names battle to secure FedExCup future Sky Sports
Golf.copy:
England’s Marco Penge bolstered his hopes of retaining full status on the PGA Tour for next season by grabbing a share of the halfway lead at the RSM Classic. Penge started the week 120th in the FedExCup standings and requiring at least a top-four finish to break inside the top 100 and guarantee full playing status on the PGA Tour in 2027.

A birdie-birdie finish saw Penge post a second-round 65 on the Stadium Course, one of two used at Sea Island Golf Club, leaving him in a four-way tie on nine under alongside Michael Thorbjornsen and Denmark's Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen.
